items.text: Relevant material is scattered across Scholar, PubMed, arXiv, conferences, RSS, email and colleague messages.
items.rationale: One canonical intake over heterogeneous sources lets coverage be tracked across all of them.

items.text: Alert streams overlap; only a minority of items matter.
items.rationale: Normalized alert items can be deduplicated by resolving which ones name the same work.

items.text: Search results show what was found, never what was missed.
items.rationale: A coverage map records what the search touched and what it never reached.

items.text: A paper is treated as new even when it was read three years ago.
items.rationale: Resolving the work's identity against a ledger of past reads prevents treating it as new again.

items.text: Synonym substitution changes result sets wholesale.
items.rationale: Surface synonyms must resolve to one canonical concept before ranking, so result sets stay stable.

items.text: Cross-disciplinary terminology breaks recall.
items.rationale: Cross-field aliases of one concept need a shared identity behind a normalized vocabulary.

items.text: Foundational, incremental, replication and critique work are mixed into one relevance ranking.
items.rationale: A typed coverage map separates foundational, replication and critique roles instead of one blended ranking.

items.text: Citation count is conflated with usefulness for the current question.
items.rationale: Relevance claims need receipts stating basis and coverage rather than a raw citation-count proxy.

items.text: Conference, preprint and journal versions enter the reading queue as separate items.
items.rationale: Conference, preprint and journal versions are one object and must resolve to a single queue entry.

items.text: Saving outpaces reading.
items.rationale: A coverage map of read versus unread makes the growing backlog explicit.

items.text: The reason a paper was saved is not recorded, so its purpose is lost months later.
items.rationale: Recording why an item entered the queue preserves its purpose as provenance.

items.text: Important, interesting and maybe-useful items share one folder.
items.rationale: Priority is a per-item state that a ledger keeps instead of one undifferentiated folder.

items.text: Abstract-only versus full-read versus figure-check versus re-derived computation are not distinguished.
items.rationale: Depth of processing is a state transition that a ledger can record per item.

items.text: Priority does not re-rank with the active project.
items.rationale: Resurfacing re-ranks queued items when the active project context changes.

items.text: An old paper that becomes relevant again does not resurface.
items.rationale: Resurfacing returns old items at the moment they become relevant again.

items.text: DOI, arXiv ID, PMID, OpenAlex ID and publisher URL are several names for one object.
items.rationale: Several identifiers naming one work is the canonical identity problem.

items.text: Preprints and versions of record are not reliably merged.
items.rationale: Preprint to version-of-record is one identity plus a version state chain.

items.text: Conference and extended journal versions are hard to pair.
items.rationale: Pairing conference and extended journal versions is identity resolution across manifestations.

items.text: Correction, erratum and retraction notices are hard to trace to the original.
items.rationale: Notices must resolve to the same work and stay linked to the original artifact.

items.text: Supplementary material is detached from the main text.
items.rationale: Supplements and main text are separate artifacts that need an explicit link.

items.text: Book chapters, books, theses and proceedings are mis-matched by metadata matchers.
items.rationale: Metadata matchers fail at identity resolution for non-journal object types.

items.text: Author name variants, renames and Chinese name inversion split one person.
items.rationale: Name variants, renames and inversions are several representations of one person.

items.text: Publisher PDF, author manuscript and preprint are several binaries of one work.
items.rationale: Several binaries of one work must resolve to a single identity.

items.text: A merged item in the reference manager leaves stale embedded citations in the Word document.
items.rationale: Embedded citations must stay linked to the manager identity so merges can be diffed for staleness.

items.text: Open-access copies exist in several places; which one is best is unclear.
items.rationale: Copies first resolve to one work; the best-copy judgment automation cannot make goes to a human queue.

items.text: A publisher 403 does not distinguish paywall, bot wall and transient failure.
items.rationale: Failures need typed receipts that distinguish paywall, bot wall and transient causes.

items.text: Institutional proxy URLs break across devices.
items.rationale: Proxy-wrapped URLs must normalize to one canonical target across devices.

items.text: Supplementary archives, code and data sit on unrelated hosts.
items.rationale: Supplementary archives, code and data on unrelated hosts need links back to the work.

items.text: Source pages rot; archive snapshots have no lineage to the current version.
items.rationale: Snapshots need lineage to the live version, and a watcher reports when the source rots.

items.text: Two-column reading order is reconstructed incorrectly.
items.rationale: Parsing must produce one canonical document object with correct reading order.

items.text: OCR destroys formulas, subscripts, superscripts and Greek letters.
items.rationale: Formula and symbol fidelity is a normalization-quality problem from OCR output to canonical text.

items.text: Tables look fine visually and fall apart on copy.
items.rationale: Table structure must be normalized and then verified deterministically, not trusted visually.

items.text: Some data exist only inside figures, without raw numbers.
items.rationale: Figure-embedded data must be normalized into the canonical numeric object.

items.text: Footnotes and endnotes are dropped by parsers.
items.rationale: Normalization must record what it extracted and what it dropped as coverage.

items.text: A claim's method details span main text, methods, appendix and a GitHub repository.
items.rationale: One claim's details span text, appendix and repository and need cross-artifact links.

items.text: Note-taking becomes a second job.
items.rationale: Automatic normalization and linking of captured material removes the manual second job.

items.text: Notes are taken and the paper is still re-read later.
items.rationale: Notes must resurface when the paper is revisited, otherwise re-reading is inevitable.

items.text: Excerpts lose page, section and context.
items.rationale: Excerpts need provenance: page, section and surrounding context.

items.text: Paraphrase, after time, cannot be told apart from the author's original words.
items.rationale: Provenance must record whether wording is quotation or paraphrase.

items.text: One claim copied into several project notes diverges.
items.rationale: Copies of one claim must keep one identity so divergence can be diffed.

items.text: Tag taxonomies grow until their owner stops using them.
items.rationale: Free-form tags need normalization into a governed canonical vocabulary.

items.text: Topic tags cannot express supports, contradicts, method or example relations.
items.rationale: Supports, contradicts, method and example are typed links between artifacts, not topic tags.

items.text: Notes freeze the understanding of the year they were written.
items.rationale: Understanding evolves; notes should be a ledger of states, not a frozen snapshot.

items.text: Outdated facts and changed interpretations are not distinguished.
items.rationale: Distinguishing outdated facts from changed interpretations needs versioned states and diffs.

items.text: A remembered claim cannot be located in a known paper.
items.rationale: A remembered claim must be linked to its exact passage in the source.

items.text: The supporting passage of a citation cannot be found.
items.rationale: Every citation needs a link to its supporting passage.

items.text: Citation-of-citation replaces reading the original source.
items.rationale: Citation chains are lineage; reaching the original is a provenance walk.

items.text: A citation supports half a sentence, not the assertion it is attached to.
items.rationale: A receipt must state exactly which span of a claim a source covers.

items.text: Secondary citations drop the qualifiers of the original.
items.rationale: Qualifiers are provenance metadata that must travel with the claim as part of its receipt.

items.text: Corrections and retractions do not propagate to old drafts.
items.rationale: A watcher on cited works plus links to drafts lets corrections and retractions propagate.

items.text: A number copied through reviews loses its source.
items.rationale: A copied number must carry its provenance through every transcription.

items.text: Numbers in figures disagree with numbers in text.
items.rationale: Figure-versus-text number agreement is computable and should be verified by diff, not by eye.

items.text: The same term means different things in different fields.
items.rationale: One surface form denoting different concepts per field is an identity-resolution failure.

items.text: Definitions drift over decades.
items.rationale: Definitions are states over time; drift must be recorded and diffed.

items.text: A new paper renames an old concept.
items.rationale: A renamed concept is a new representation of an old identity.

items.text: Abbreviations collide.
items.rationale: Colliding abbreviations must be resolved to distinct identities by context.

items.text: Formula symbols coincide while definitions differ.
items.rationale: Identical symbols with different definitions are distinct identities sharing a representation.

items.text: A default assumption of one field does not hold in another.
items.rationale: Receipts must state the field assumptions a result depends on so they do not port silently.

items.text: Not finding something is mistaken for nobody having done it.
items.rationale: A coverage map separates searched-and-absent from never-searched.

items.text: English-only search produces fake novelty.
items.rationale: Language coverage must be explicit so English-only absence is not read as novelty.

items.text: Theses, proceedings and preprints are skipped.
items.rationale: Coverage must name which literatures were and were not searched.

items.text: Old terminology hides historical work from retrieval.
items.rationale: Historical aliases must resolve to the canonical concept so old work can be retrieved.

items.text: A little-known paper may have already filled the claimed gap.
items.rationale: A gap claim needs a coverage map plus a receipt of what was checked.

items.text: Absence of research and inconsistency of results are conflated.
items.rationale: Coverage distinguishes absence of studies from conflicting ones, and receipts record the conflict.

items.text: Methods sections are too brief.
items.rationale: Unreported parameters must be marked unknown on a coverage map and routed to a human queue.

items.text: Key parameters hide in supplements.
items.rationale: Parameters in supplements need links between main text and supplementary artifacts.

items.text: Reagent versions, software versions and random seeds are missing.
items.rationale: Required reporting fields compile into checks, and a coverage map shows which are missing.

items.text: Preprocessing is described incompletely.
items.rationale: Preprocessing completeness is a checklist compiled into checks over a coverage map.

items.text: Paper defaults and repository defaults differ.
items.rationale: Paper versus repository defaults is a diff between two states.

items.text: Methods cite other methods, requiring recursive lookup.
items.rationale: Recursive method citations are a link graph that must be traversable.

items.text: Following-X descriptions conceal actual modifications.
items.rationale: A following-X claim must be diffed against X to expose actual modifications.

items.text: Protocol changes during the experiment are not versioned in the publication.
items.rationale: Protocol evolution during the experiment is a state history the publication must reflect.

items.text: Exclusion criteria are scattered.
items.rationale: Scattered criteria must be linked and normalized into one canonical list.

items.text: Work happens at the bench; records are written in the evening.
items.rationale: Provenance must be captured at the bench, not reconstructed in the evening.

items.text: Failed experiments are the least recorded.
items.rationale: Coverage must include failed experiments, and the ledger must record them as states.

items.text: One protocol exists as paper, Word and Notion copies.
items.rationale: Paper, Word and Notion copies are representations of one protocol that must normalize to one object.

items.text: Raw-data file names cannot be traced to experiments.
items.rationale: Raw files need provenance links to the experiments that produced them.

items.text: Sample IDs and notebook IDs are disconnected.
items.rationale: Sample IDs and notebook IDs are disconnected artifacts that need an explicit link.

items.text: A figure cannot be traced to the analysis run that produced it.
items.rationale: A figure must carry lineage to the analysis run that produced it.

items.text: The rationale of a past decision is absent.
items.rationale: Decisions need their rationale recorded as decision provenance.

items.text: Negative results and abandoned attempts disappear and are repeated later.
items.rationale: Abandoned attempts must be ledgered and resurfaced before they are repeated.

items.text: Experimental conditions live only in one researcher's memory.
items.rationale: Conditions held in one memory must be externalized as provenance records.

items.text: Raw, cleaned and analysis-ready states are confused.
items.rationale: Raw, cleaned and analysis-ready are states of one dataset and need a ledger.

items.text: Spreadsheet software silently retypes CSV columns.
items.rationale: Silent column retyping is caught by deterministic schema verification, not by inspection.

items.text: Units are inconsistent.
items.rationale: Units must normalize to canonical form and conversions must be verified.

items.text: Missing values mix 0, NA, blank and 999.
items.rationale: Mixed sentinel encodings for missing values must normalize to one canonical representation.

items.text: Column names change between batches.
items.rationale: Column names must map to a canonical schema and batch-to-batch changes must be diffed.

items.text: The codebook is separated from the dataset.
items.rationale: Codebook and dataset are separate artifacts that must stay linked.

items.text: Exclusion decisions leave no ledger.
items.rationale: Exclusion decisions are state transitions and belong in a ledger.

items.text: Cleaning is irreversible.
items.rationale: Keeping the transition history makes cleaning reversible.

items.text: Provenance is lost on copy and paste.
items.rationale: Copy and paste must carry provenance with the data.

items.text: File names accumulate: final.csv, final2.csv, really_final.csv.
items.rationale: Version proliferation by filename is a missing state ledger over dataset versions.

items.text: Reported p values and statistics do not match.
items.rationale: Reported statistics are recomputable; verification must not trust the text.

items.text: Confidence intervals disagree with estimates.
items.rationale: Confidence intervals are recomputable from estimates and must be checked deterministically.

items.text: Percentage denominators change without note.
items.rationale: Denominators are checkable, and receipts must state which denominator each percentage uses.

items.text: N differs between abstract, tables and flowchart.
items.rationale: N across abstract, tables and flowchart is a numeric consistency check.

items.text: SD and SE are interchanged.
items.rationale: SD/SE confusion is partially checkable; genuinely ambiguous cases go to a human queue.

items.text: One-tailed and two-tailed are unspecified.
items.rationale: Receipts must state test sidedness, and reporting rules must compile into checks.

items.text: Multiple-testing correction is unclear.
items.rationale: Whether and how multiplicity was corrected must be stated on the receipt.

items.text: Transformed and raw scales are mixed.
items.rationale: Scales must normalize before comparison, and mixing must be caught by verification.

items.text: Effect-size definitions are ambiguous.
items.rationale: Effect-size claims must carry their exact definition on the receipt.

items.text: Graph-only values require digitization.
items.rationale: Digitization normalizes graph pixels to numbers with uncertainty routed to a queue.

items.text: Statistical package defaults change across versions.
items.rationale: Default changes across package versions must be diffed and watched.

items.text: The query cannot be reproduced exactly.
items.rationale: The query must be recorded as provenance and compiled into a re-runnable form.

items.text: Database export formats are mutually incompatible.
items.rationale: Incompatible exports must normalize into one canonical record format.

items.text: Deduplication kills genuinely distinct papers and misses version duplicates.
items.rationale: Deduplication is identity resolution: keep distinct papers, merge version duplicates.

items.text: Title and abstract screening is mechanical.
items.rationale: Eligibility criteria compile into screening checks, with uncertain items queued for humans.

items.text: Exclusion reasons are backfilled, weakening the ledger.
items.rationale: Exclusion reasons must be ledger entries written at decision time, not backfilled.

items.text: Missing full texts bias selection.
items.rationale: Missing full texts must appear on the coverage map as unscreened.

items.text: Multiple reports of one study are counted as multiple studies.
items.rationale: Multiple reports of one study resolve to one study identity.

items.text: One cohort across several papers is double counted.
items.rationale: One cohort across several papers is one identity and must be counted once.

items.text: Arms, units and time points are extracted incorrectly.
items.rationale: Extracted arms, units and time points must be verified against source tables after normalization.

items.text: Data are read off graphs by hand.
items.rationale: Reading graphs is normalization whose uncertainty belongs in a queue.

items.text: Effect directions are inverted.
items.rationale: Effect-direction inversion is a sign error that deterministic checks can catch.

items.text: Reviewer disagreement in extraction is hard to trace.
items.rationale: Disagreements go to an explicit queue and their resolutions are ledgered.

items.text: Meta-analysis inputs cannot be traced back to the paper's tables.
items.rationale: Every meta-analysis input needs lineage back to the paper's tables.

items.text: Transcripts and audio timestamps are disconnected.
items.rationale: Transcript spans and audio timestamps are artifacts that need links.

items.text: Interview to open code to axial code to theme lineage is weak.
items.rationale: Interview to open code to axial code to theme is lineage and must be recorded as such.

items.text: The codebook changes during analysis.
items.rationale: A changing codebook is a state history, not an overwrite.

items.text: Merged codes lose the reason old segments were reclassified.
items.rationale: Merges must record reclassification reasons as provenance on state transitions.

items.text: Inter-coder disagreement is not kept in structured form.
items.rationale: Inter-coder disagreement belongs in a structured queue with ledgered resolutions.

items.text: Negative and disconfirming cases drown in the main narrative.
items.rationale: Negative cases must stay on the coverage map and resurface against the main narrative.

items.text: Participant attributes are disconnected from quotes.
items.rationale: Quotes need links to participant attributes.

items.text: Anonymization destroys analytic context.
items.rationale: Pseudonymized canonical objects can keep analytic links while stripping identity.

items.text: A repository exists without an exact commit.
items.rationale: Provenance must pin the exact commit that produced the results.

items.text: Requirements are unpinned.
items.rationale: Pinned requirements are environment provenance.

items.text: CUDA, Python and package matrices are brittle.
items.rationale: Environment matrices compile into executable checks that verify the toolchain.

items.text: Dataset download links die.
items.rationale: Dead download links are state changes a watcher must report.

items.text: The dataset version is unknown.
items.rationale: The dataset version is provenance that must be recorded.

items.text: Checkpoints do not match the paper.
items.rationale: Checkpoint behavior must be verified and diffed against reported results.

items.text: Preprocessing is hidden.
items.rationale: Hidden preprocessing is missing lineage in the pipeline.

items.text: Random seeds are unpublished.
items.rationale: Unpublished seeds are missing run provenance.

items.text: Evaluation scripts differ from descriptions.
items.rationale: Evaluation scripts must be diffed against their descriptions and verified to match.

items.text: Numerical behavior depends on hardware.
items.rationale: Hardware-sensitive results need verification within tolerance plus an environment receipt.

items.text: Notebook cells do not record actual execution order.
items.rationale: Execution order is a state history the notebook must record as lineage.

items.text: Shell commands work only on the author's machine.
items.rationale: Portability rules compile into checks that run the commands in a clean environment.

items.text: Absolute paths are hard-coded.
items.rationale: Hard-coded absolute paths are a rule-checkable defect.

items.text: External APIs and databases change after publication.
items.rationale: External APIs and databases must be watched for post-publication change.

items.text: Published code contains inference but not training.
items.rationale: What a release contains and omits is a coverage question.

items.text: Notebooks run once and cannot rerun.
items.rationale: Rerunnability is verified deterministically against recorded provenance.

items.text: Manual dataframe edits leave code unaware.
items.rationale: Manual edits are untracked state transitions that a ledger plus diff would expose.

items.text: Figures do not record generation parameters.
items.rationale: Generation parameters are figure provenance.

items.text: Post-hoc Illustrator edits break the figure-data link.
items.rationale: Post-hoc edits break the lineage link between figure and data.

items.text: Manuscript tables are copied by hand and go stale.
items.rationale: Tables must be live links to data, and staleness detected by diff.

items.text: Report numbers come from an old model version.
items.rationale: Reported numbers need lineage to the model version that produced them.

items.text: Rounding errors accumulate across copies.
items.rationale: Rounding consistency across copies is a deterministic numeric check.

items.text: The latest version is unknown.
items.rationale: A state ledger over document versions makes latest unambiguous.

items.text: PI annotates in Word, the student edits in Overleaf, and the two diverge.
items.rationale: Two editing streams must normalize to one canonical document and be diffed.

items.text: Key decisions in Slack and email never enter project records.
items.rationale: Decisions in chat and email must be ingested and normalized into the project record with provenance.

items.text: Departing students leave data nobody can find.
items.rationale: Data must be linked to the project registry so it survives personnel changes.

items.text: A collaborator changes a column without a reason.
items.rationale: Every change is a ledger entry that carries its reason.

items.text: Permissions leave results accessible to one person.
items.rationale: Access coverage, meaning who can reach which result, must be recorded.

items.text: Newcomers do not know which routes were tried and failed.
items.rationale: Failed routes must be ledgered and resurfaced for newcomers.

items.text: Handoffs contain files but no decision history.
items.rationale: Handoffs need decision provenance and a state history, not bare files.

items.text: Claims are written first and citations hunted afterwards.
items.rationale: Claims and citations must be linked at writing time, not hunted afterwards.

items.text: Papers update after citations are added; claims do not sync.
items.rationale: Cited papers must be watched so updates propagate to dependent claims.

items.text: Similar claims in an introduction draw on duplicated literature.
items.rationale: Duplicated claims must resolve to one identity with consolidated links to the literature.

items.text: Methods drift from the actual code.
items.rationale: Methods text must be linked to code and diffed against it.

items.text: Results drift from tables and figures.
items.rationale: Results text must be verified and diffed against tables and figures.

items.text: Abstract numbers do not track body revisions.
items.rationale: Abstract numbers must be verified and diffed against the body.

items.text: Limitations are written late and omit known caveats.
items.rationale: Caveats recorded as receipts must resurface when limitations are written.

items.text: Terminology is inconsistent across sections.
items.rationale: Terminology must normalize to a canonical set and consistency must be verified.

items.text: A missing analysis is discovered late in the manuscript.
items.rationale: A coverage map of planned analyses surfaces a missing one before submission.

items.text: Journal requirements differ per venue.
items.rationale: Venue requirements are rules that must compile into executable checks.

items.text: Transfer means redoing citations, word limits, sections and figures.
items.rationale: A canonical manuscript plus compiled venue rules makes transfer a regeneration, not a redo.

items.text: The reporting guideline is chosen wrongly.
items.rationale: Guideline selection follows from compiled rules; ambiguous fits go to a human queue.

items.text: CONSORT, STROBE and PRISMA items are completed just before submission.
items.rationale: Reporting checklists compile into checks whose coverage is tracked from project start.

items.text: Author contributions, conflicts and data availability are filled at the end.
items.rationale: Contributions and conflicts are facts to ledger as they happen, not reconstruct at the end.

items.text: Blinded manuscripts leak author identity.
items.rationale: Identity leaks in blinded manuscripts are deterministically checkable.

items.text: Supplementary naming and cross-references are wrong.
items.rationale: Naming and cross-reference correctness is rule-checkable.

items.text: Figure DPI, size and fonts fail the target format.
items.rationale: Figure format rules compile into checks verified before submission.

items.text: Reference metadata errors accumulate in bulk.
items.rationale: Reference metadata is verifiable against registries in bulk.

items.text: Reviewer comments and manuscript revisions have no one-to-one mapping.
items.rationale: Each comment needs a one-to-one link to its revision.

items.text: Multiple reviewers raise the same issue.
items.rationale: The same issue raised by two reviewers is one identity and should merge.

items.text: Reviewer A and B demand conflicting changes.
items.rationale: Conflicting demands cannot be auto-resolved and belong in a human queue.

items.text: Line locators in the response letter go stale after revision.
items.rationale: Locators must be links into the text so revisions can diff and update them.

items.text: A claimed fix misses a second occurrence of the same text.
items.rationale: A fix must be verified over all occurrences, with coverage showing what was checked.

items.text: A reviewer-suggested citation may itself be irrelevant.
items.rationale: A suggested citation needs an evidence receipt, and doubtful relevance goes to a human queue.

items.text: Second rounds cannot confirm whether old issues actually closed.
items.rationale: Issue open and closed is a state ledger that later rounds can query.

items.text: Checking whether citations support claims is slow.
items.rationale: Claim-support checking needs receipts that bind citations to spans.

items.text: Suspicious table values require hand calculation.
items.rationale: Suspicious values are recomputable and should be verified, not hand-calculated.

items.text: Overlap with an author's earlier work is hard to batch-check.
items.rationale: Overlap checking is a diff across an author's resolved body of work.

items.text: Data and code availability links are checked one by one.
items.rationale: Availability links are checkable automatically and watched over time.

items.text: Methods omissions have no automatic checklist.
items.rationale: Methods checklists compile into checks over a coverage map of sections.

items.text: Self-citation patterns across 350 references are inspected by eye.
items.rationale: Self-citation counting is deterministic once author identities are resolved.

items.text: Funding opportunity and agency instructions change.
items.rationale: Instruction changes are future state changes a watcher must report.

items.text: Template versions expire.
items.rationale: Template expiry is a state change to watch.

items.text: Page, font, header, footer and URL rules are fragmented.
items.rationale: Fragmented format rules must compile into one executable check set.

items.text: Biosketches and current-and-pending are re-entered each time.
items.rationale: A canonical person record resolves to one identity and regenerates each form.

items.text: Collaborators reuse outdated biosketches.
items.rationale: Biosketch staleness is a state problem plus a watch on upstream updates.

items.text: Publications are re-selected per proposal.
items.rationale: Proposal-relevant publications must resurface by context instead of manual re-selection.

items.text: The data management plan does not match the actual workflow.
items.rationale: Plan versus actual workflow is a diff.

items.text: One institutional datum is copied into several attachments.
items.rationale: One institutional datum copied into attachments must normalize to one canonical source.

items.text: Format errors surface only at the submission portal.
items.rationale: Portal format rules must compile into local checks that run before submission.

items.text: Resubmission cannot map reviewer criticism to changed proposal text.
items.rationale: Criticisms must link to proposal text so changes can be mapped and diffed.

items.text: University templates conflict with Word and LaTeX defaults.
items.rationale: Template requirements are rules that compile into checks over the document.

items.text: Section breaks and page numbering consume mechanical hours.
items.rationale: Section breaks and page numbering are mechanical and must be automated and verified.

items.text: Published chapters and dissertation versions drift apart.
items.rationale: Chapter and dissertation versions are identities whose drift must be diffed.

items.text: Figure and table lists have omissions.
items.rationale: List completeness is verifiable against a coverage map of figures and tables.

items.text: Format checks are highly local per institution.
items.rationale: Institution-local format checks are compiled rules, not folklore.

items.text: Code and data stop being maintained after publication.
items.rationale: Maintenance decay after publication is a state change a watcher must surface.

items.text: DOIs stay alive while external links rot.
items.rationale: Link rot under stable DOIs is exactly what a watcher reports.

items.text: Dependencies disappear.
items.rationale: Dependency disappearance is a state change to watch.

items.text: Corrections do not notify local citers.
items.rationale: Corrections must be watched and propagated along links to local citers.

items.text: Systematic reviews go stale within two years.
items.rationale: Reviews go stale as new evidence appears; a watcher reports the drift.

items.text: New dataset versions change conclusions while old analyses remain unaware.
items.rationale: New dataset versions must be watched and their effect diffed against old analyses.

items.text: Lecture, notes and flashcards mean entering the same content three times.
items.rationale: Lecture, notes and cards are representations of one content identity and should be authored once in canonical form.

items.text: PDF, video, handouts and exercises are isolated.
items.rationale: Isolated media types must normalize and link into one artifact graph.

items.text: One concept's treatments across materials are not merged.
items.rationale: Treatments of one concept across materials must resolve to one identity and be linked.

items.text: Cards are detached from the context that produced them.
items.rationale: Cards need provenance links to the context that produced them.

items.text: Image-based knowledge is slow to turn into occlusion cards.
items.rationale: Image content must normalize into card-ready canonical form.

items.text: Recognition is mistaken for recall.
items.rationale: Recognition and recall are distinct performance states; practice must adapt to which one failed.

items.text: Recognition is mistaken for generation and application.
items.rationale: Generation and application are distinct states that practice must target separately.

items.text: Flashcard performance does not transfer to real problems.
items.rationale: Transfer failure is a failure type the practice engine must answer from ledgered performance.

items.text: The final answer is known but the intermediate reasoning is not.
items.rationale: Step-level reasoning needs ledgered states and a coverage map, not a single final-answer bit.

items.text: Prerequisite holes are invisible.
items.rationale: Prerequisite holes are unknowns a coverage map must expose.

items.text: Wrong answers record the answer, not the error mechanism.
items.rationale: Errors must be ledgered by mechanism so practice can adapt to the failure type.

items.text: Confusable concepts are reviewed separately.
items.rationale: Confusables must resolve as distinct identities and be practiced by discrimination.

items.text: The review backlog grows without bound.
items.rationale: Unbounded backlog is a scheduling problem the practice engine owns.

items.text: All content receives the same spaced-repetition policy.
items.rationale: One policy for all content ignores per-item failure history; practice must adapt.

items.text: A proof attempt cannot locate the failing step.
items.rationale: Proof steps are checkable; locating the failing step drives the next practice action.

items.text: Reading the solution immediately produces an illusion of mastery.
items.rationale: Practice must require generation before showing solutions to prevent fluency illusions.

items.text: Full solutions destroy productive struggle.
items.rationale: Hint granularity is a practice-engine decision that preserves productive struggle.

items.text: No one judges proof rigor.
items.rationale: Rule-based rigor checks run deterministically; the rest queue for a human judge.

items.text: The same error recurs without a misconception identity.
items.rationale: Recurring errors must resolve to one misconception identity that practice then targets.

items.text: There is no graduated hint that reveals only the next step.
items.rationale: Graduated next-step hints are the practice engine's delivery mechanism.

items.text: Textbook examples are solved, variants are not.
items.rationale: Failure on variants is a failure type that should drive variant practice.

items.text: Flashcard recall does not become language production.
items.rationale: Recall-to-production gaps are a failure type requiring production practice.

items.text: Isolated facts are trained without contextual retrieval.
items.rationale: Facts must be resurfaced in context and practiced contextually.

items.text: No progression from near transfer to far transfer.
items.rationale: Near-to-far progression is a sequenced practice policy.

items.text: Method selection for a new problem is never trained.
items.rationale: Method selection is a trainable skill the engine must schedule.

items.text: Learners judge their own mastery poorly.
items.rationale: Objective performance states diffed against self-judgment expose miscalibration.

items.text: Familiarity from easy repetition masquerades as learning.
items.rationale: Easy repetition must be detected from ledgered performance and replaced with effortful practice.

items.text: Time is spent reviewing what is already known.
items.rationale: Already-known content is visible on a coverage map, and scheduling should skip it.

items.text: The true cause of failure, knowledge gap versus retrieval failure versus strategy choice, is unknown.
items.rationale: Failure-cause attribution is the engine's diagnosis step over ledgered history.
